title: Why Can't You Raise Just ONE Eyebrow? 🤨
description:
Try to raise just one of your eyebrows: for most people both go up. Each half of your brain sends its "lift" signal to the muscles above BOTH brows, so the two tend to rise as a pair, while your mouth gets a separate line to each side, which is why half a smile is easy. That double wiring is so reliable that after a stroke on one side of the brain, the forehead usually still lifts on both sides, and doctors check for exactly that. Some people can lift one brow anyway, and nobody is quite sure why; holding the other one down with a finger is the classic way to practise. Could you raise just one? Yes or no?
